title: SEBI Deploys AI and Rural Outreach to Combat Finfluencer Misinformation
excerpt: India's market regulator is expanding investor education to panchayats and WhatsApp while its AI tool Sudarshan has already taken down 1.2 lakh misleading social media posts.
body:
• SEBI's annual report reveals a sweeping expansion of investor education, including rural outreach to panchayats and AI-powered WhatsApp campaigns in multiple languages
  • The regulator has removed over 1.2 lakh misleading social media posts by unregistered financial influencers using its AI tool Sudarshan
  • A SEBI survey found that 62% of Indian investors rely on financial influencers for some or most of their investment decisions
  • From May 2026, all SEBI-registered entities must display their registration numbers on every social media post, making verification easier

The Finfluencer Problem

India's Securities and Exchange Board has laid out an aggressive plan to expand investor education from AI-powered surveillance of social media to grassroots outreach in rural panchayats, according to the regulator's latest annual report and recent disclosures.

The push comes as SEBI confronts a troubling reality: 62% of Indian investors rely on financial influencers — commonly known as finfluencers — for some or most of their investment decisions, according to the SEBI Investor Survey 2025. In rural areas, the dependence is even higher, with 62% of equity investors citing social media influencers as a key source of investment guidance.

Sudarshan: SEBI's AI Weapon

At the center of SEBI's enforcement strategy is Sudarshan, an in-house artificial intelligence tool capable of scanning multilingual audio, video, and text content across social media platforms to detect violations.

"We have removed more than 120,000 such pieces of content from social media where we found egregious behaviour violating our norms."

— Tuhin Kanta Pandey, SEBI Chairman

Chairman Pandey told ANI that SEBI's regulations clearly mandate investment advice can only come from registered entities. The regulator has drawn a firm line between financial education — protected as free expression — and misleading investment advice that targets unsophisticated investors.

The AI-led approach represents a significant shift from manual monitoring. SEBI can now track content at scale across platforms, flagging everything from overt stock calls to coded references like ticker symbols paired with rocket emojis.

From Digital to Doorstep

Beyond technology, SEBI is expanding its reach to India's villages. The annual report outlines plans for investor education campaigns through panchayats — local self-governing bodies that serve as the primary administrative unit in rural India.

The regulator is also deploying WhatsApp-based awareness campaigns for safe investing, meeting investors where they already communicate. These campaigns will be available in multiple languages, addressing the challenge of reaching India's linguistically diverse retail investor base.

The rural outreach is significant because the SEBI survey found sharp differences in information sources by geography and income. Among investors in the top nine metropolitan areas, reliance on peers and influencers is relatively lower at 51%, with greater use of market analysis reports. But in smaller towns and rural areas, friends, family, and social media influencers dominate investment decision-making.

Regulatory Tightening

SEBI has also tightened compliance requirements for registered intermediaries. Since May 2026, all SEBI-registered entities must display their registered name and registration number at the top of any content — including videos — posted on social media platforms, including YouTube.

The regulator has partnered with Google to verify investing apps, with more than 600 apps including Zerodha and Groww now carrying verification badges on the Google Play Store. An estimated 66 fake financial apps have been removed from platforms.

The impact on the creator economy has been substantial. Industry estimates suggest that SEBI's restrictions on the use of live market data in unregistered educational content have affected 45 to 60% of finance-related brand collaborations.

The Bigger Picture

SEBI's annual report also outlines plans for faster approvals of alternative investment fund schemes, corporate bond tokenization, and broader regulatory modernization in FY27. The regulator is pursuing what Chairman Pandey has described as a "calibrated, surgical approach" to market regulation rather than heavy-handed intervention.

For the more than 15 crore demat account holders in India — and the growing number of NRI investors managing portfolios remotely — the combination of AI surveillance, rural education, and tighter registration requirements represents SEBI's most comprehensive attempt yet to clean up the gap between legitimate financial education and predatory investment advice.
nri_angle: NRI investors managing Indian portfolios remotely are particularly vulnerable to finfluencer misinformation and will benefit from SEBI's enhanced digital monitoring.
